top_strength: The pricing and packing handling was genuinely strong, and the estimate was tailored rather than canned. She gave the day-tiered rate with the inclusions in one clean breath — 'hourly rate during Saturdays is $230 for two guys. Everything's already included there gas and the truck taxes and insurance' — then adjusted the baseline for the actual job instead of quoting the generic one: 'moving a one bedroom apartment typically takes two and a half to three and a half hours with you guys. But if you're moving from a fort floor to another fort floor unit, I would estimate it to take about about three to four hours.' That is exactly the behavior the estimate-accuracy push needs. She also handled a multi-part packing question without getting flustered, corrected the customer's own math when he doubled the hours, and volunteered the money-saving answer unprompted: 'No, we can definitely use your boxes if you have the packing supplies to.' Best rapport moment was the spam-call worry — the customer said he did not want to be chased, and she killed it flat: 'Oh, no, no, no, not at all. We don't, we don't do that,' then explained the only call he would get is the movers on move day. He came back with 'Okay, that's good.'
coaching_note: The single highest-value fix is the close. This customer was ready — 'Okay, sounds good' on the price, no objections, a firm October 3rd date, and he asked for the email himself — and the call ended with 'if you have any questions just let us know or if you're ready to move forward with us just give us a call.' A warm one-bedroom on a confirmed date was handed back to the customer as homework. The line needed was: 'We've got Saturday the 3rd open right now and there's no deposit to hold it — want me to go ahead and lock that in for you?' She already had the no-deposit differentiator in hand and used it one sentence too late, as a fact about the company rather than as the reason to say yes today. Attach the email verification ask to the same breath — 'I'll send that over now, take a look and reply if anything's off' — which costs four seconds and would have fired the email-handoff flag. Second priority, and it is cheap: the three differentiators never came up at all. No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee are about twenty seconds combined, and this customer is price-shopping a one-bedroom where every mover in Austin quotes a similar hourly rate. Right now he has nothing to compare the next quote against except the number. Third, Save Your Ass is worth real money on this specific move: two fourth-floor units mean walk distance drives the bill, and a prep speech — consolidate the loose items, take a carload yourself — would shorten a three-to-four hour job measurably.
phone_presence_notes: Polite, patient and responsive — the repeated 'Oh, no, no, no, not at all' reassurance on the spam-call worry and the unprompted 'we can definitely use your boxes' both land as real warmth, but the rest is efficient intake with almost no affirmations, no 'how are you today', and the name used only three times in eight and a half minutes.
